Q: Not all the groups are visible in Telethon A:

GetDialogsRequest is a raw request and Telegram has a maximum limit of 100 for it. You should not use it, and you should always prefer to use client.get_dialogs(). You can check if it's a group with dialog.is_group, and a channel with dialog.is_channel. So, for megagroups:

if dialog.is_group and dialog.is_channel:
    # it's a megagroup (= supergroup)

The attributes can be found in the documentation at https://docs.telethon.dev/en/stable/modules/custom.html#telethon.tl.custom.dialog.Dialog.

Q: How can I format a duration with std::println? A:

I was expecting a duration of exactly 1 year without fractional seconds,

Extracting the internal count() from a duration, is often dangerous and unnecessary with std::chrono types. If a code change alters the duration's period, you will start getting incorrect values.

The following will give you a year count regardless of the internal representation of your duration.

The code is also smaller and arguably clearer.

    auto duration = tp2 - tp1;
    std::println("duration: {} year(s)", duration / years{1});

The lesson: dividing two durations gives you a correct count without needing to know (or duration_cast) either duration's representation.

See it work.

Note also that you can get a floting point result by making either duration floating point.

    std::println("duration: {} year(s)", 1.0 * duration / years{1});

See it work.

Q: How to upgrade MongoDB? A:

Shutdown mongodb with:

/usr/bin/mongodb --config $PATH-TO-CONFIG --shutdown

replace /usr/bin with the right directory. Copy new mongodb and restart mongodb afterwards.

Q: Find height of circle where visible area (not covered by rectangles) is half the total area A:

This is obviously an exercise from some programming class (and hence a programming question notwithstanding earlier comments). I suggest you start by considering, given the specifications of a circle and one rectangle, how to write a function that returns the amount by which the rectangle overlaps the circle. To do that, you may want subroutines that determine whether the circle intersects the left side of the rectangle, the top of the rectangle, the right-side of the rectangle, and/or the bottom of the circle, and where. Then, for each of the possible cases that result, figure out how to determine the area of the rectangle overlapped with the circle. Write code for each of those.

Then write code to use that to handle multiple rectangles. If they can overlap, figure out how to deal with that. Add some code that finds the area of the circle above the horizon and subtracts the amount overlapped with the rectangles.

Once you have done that, you will have a function that returns the visible area given the height of the sun. Then you need to find the height that produces the desired visible area. That part is a fairly straightforward numerical-solution-finding algorithm, which I expect has been covered previously in class. The function is monotonic, so a simple binary search would work.
